title: Russia wins first winter Paralympic gold medal for 12 years
content:
Varvara Voronchikhina has won Russia’s first winter Paralympic gold medal for 12 years.

The 23-year-old, who was born without part of her left hand and competes in the standing classification, came out on top in the super-G with a time of 1:15.60s.

She raced second in a field of 15 athletes, posting the fastest time thanks to a flawless second-half of the 38-gate course. She hit top speeds of 85km/h in the middle section, quicker than anyone else. Crossing the finish line, she fist-pumped the air to applause.

Frenchwoman Aurelie Richard took her second silver of these Games, having also made the podium in Saturday’s downhill. Her super-G time of 1:17.56s meant she finished almost two full seconds back on Voronchikhina. Richard was quicker in the first half of the run, but lost time when she went too wide and had to cut back in to avoid missing a gate (which would have disqualified her). Bronze was won by Ebba Aarsjoe of Sweden (1:17.64s), who adds that to her downhill gold.

This is Voronchikhina’s second medal of the games — she won downhill bronze two days ago — and it is the first time that Russia have topped the podium under their own flag since the winter Paralympics on home soil in Sochi in 2014.

“It’s really special for me because I can see my flag on my friends who arrived here,” Voronchikhina said. “It’s amazing. I have a big support in my family and my friends and all people in Russia. Russia is a big country, and I have big fans here.”

She is one of six Russian athletes (plus four Belarusian cross-country skiers) given what the International Paralympic Committee (IPC) call “bipartite” entries to the Milano-Cortina Games.

They were banned in 2018 because of state-sponsored doping and again in 2022, because the IPC had evidence that they were using Para sports to promote the war following the invasion of Ukraine. Last September, IPC members voted to lift the suspension against Russia and Belarus, and following that they took FIS (the skiing and snowboard governing body) to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in December.

There, they successfully appealed the ban from alpine, cross-country skiing and snowboarding on discrimination grounds. As they had missed the qualification windows for these Paralympics — the sports governing bodies individually still prevented them competing — it was ruled, by CAS, that Russia could be given six and Belarus four automatic entries. CAS did this because they did not consider there to be a sufficient “framework” for the athletes to compete neutrally. Confirmation of Russian and Belarusian athletes competing arrived less than two weeks before the Games.

These, an IPC spokesperson told The Athletic, were specifically and only for high-level Russian athletes who would contend for medals. Voronchikhina won medals in all six events at the 2021 World Championships in Lillehammer, Norway, including golds in super combined and super-G.

The last time Russia had athletes top the podium was at their 2014 home Games, when they won the most medals (16) in Para alpine skiing and the joint-most gold medals (six, tied with Germany).
